planting.note: Pot rooted stem cuttings in spring into a chunky, well-drained aroid mix with a moss pole or totem for climbing support in bright, indirect light.

directions: Green Wonder is a long-established hybrid between the hairy-petioled Philodendron squamiferum and the deeply lobed P. pedatum, combining traits of both parents into a vigorous climbing plant with irregularly lobed, ruffled leaves. New growth emerges with a coppery-red flush inherited from the squamiferum parent before maturing to a glossy mid-green, and the fuzzy reddish petioles remain a distinguishing feature at every stage. Train it up a moss pole or bark totem to encourage larger, more deeply cut adult leaves, and keep the aroid mix evenly moist but never waterlogged. Provide bright, indirect light for the best leaf lobing and color contrast, and propagate by rooting stem cuttings with at least one node.

planting.note: Pot tissue-cultured starts or rooted cuttings into a loose, well-drained aroid mix in spring, providing a totem once vines begin to lengthen.

directions: Majesty is a mass-produced tissue-culture hybrid bred from velvet-leaved Philodendron parentage, prized for broad, quilted, deep-green heart-shaped leaves overlaid with pronounced silvery-white venation reminiscent of collector species like P. verrucosum, but on a sturdier, easier-care plant suited to typical home humidity. It holds a compact, short-vining habit in youth and benefits from a light totem as stems begin to lengthen with age. Keep it in bright, indirect light with consistent warmth, let the top inch of the aroid mix dry between waterings, and avoid cold drafts, which can cause the thin, velvety leaves to develop dark blotching. Propagate from single-node stem cuttings rooted in moist sphagnum.

planting.note: Pot rooted cuttings in spring into well-drained aroid mix in bright, indirect light; this self-heading hybrid needs no climbing support.

directions: Golden Dragon arose as a color-mutated sport of the popular self-heading hybrid Philodendron 'Painted Lady' and is maintained true-to-type only by vegetative cutting propagation, since the trait is not seed-stable. New leaves emerge a bright gold-chartreuse and gradually mature to green overlaid with irregular creamy-yellow marbling, giving each rosette a two-toned, painterly look distinct from the pale speckling of its parent cultivar. Give it bright, indirect light to hold the gold new-growth color without scorching, and rotate the pot occasionally for even growth. Keep the potting mix evenly moist but well drained, and remove old lower leaves as the clump fills out.

planting.note: Divide basal offsets or plant container-grown specimens after frost into rich, moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Hope Selloum is a long-cultivated, smaller-growing selection of tree philodendron that has been a mainstay of Gulf South foundation plantings and interiorscaping for decades, valued for staying well under the towering, trunk-forming scale of straight species selloum while keeping the same bold, deeply lobed leaf texture. It forms a dense, self-heading rosette without a significant above-ground trunk, making it easier to fit into foundation beds, shaded courtyards, and mixed border plantings. Established clumps tolerate brief light frost in zone 9, resprouting from the crown even when top growth is damaged. Divide basal offsets to propagate, and keep soil consistently moist but well drained through the growing season.

planting.note: Divide basal offsets or pot container-grown specimens in spring into rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Emerald Duke is an older, self-heading selloum-type philodendron cultivar long favored in the commercial interiorscape trade for its neat, rounded clump of glossy, deeply lobed dark-green leaves on a scale between full-sized selloum and the more compact Xanadu. It tolerates lower interior light levels better than many foliage philodendrons, which made it a staple of mall atriums and office plantscapes, and it performs equally well as a shaded landscape foundation plant in frost-free climates. Keep soil evenly moist and well drained, feed lightly during the growing season, and divide basal offsets to propagate. Established outdoor plantings recover from brief light frost by resprouting from the crown.

planting.note: Divide basal offsets or pot container-grown specimens in spring into rich, well-drained soil; brighter light than typical selloum-type philodendrons intensifies the gold leaf color.

directions: Florida Sunshine is a compact, self-heading philodendron cultivar in the Xanadu/selloum lineage, selected for foliage that emerges bright chartreuse-yellow and holds a warm gold-green color far brighter than the deep green of its relatives. It needs more light than typical shade philodendrons to keep the gold pigmentation from fading to plain green, so give it filtered sun or bright open shade rather than deep shade. The deeply lobed leaves form a tidy, rounded mound similar in scale to Xanadu, making it a good accent among darker-leaved foliage plants in mixed shade borders or large containers. Keep soil evenly moist and well drained, and divide basal offsets to propagate.

planting.note: Pot rhizome divisions in spring into a shallow, wide container of chunky, well-drained aroid mix in bright, indirect light.

directions: McDowell is a collector hybrid combining the creeping, rhizomatous growth habit of Philodendron gloriosum with the larger scale and quilted texture of P. pastazanum, producing broad, velvety, heart-shaped leaves with prominent pale venation on a plant that spreads sideways rather than climbing. Grow it in a shallow, wide pot to give the surface-creeping rhizome room to travel, and keep it out of direct sun, which can scorch the thin velvet leaf surface. Water when the top inch of mix dries out, and maintain high humidity to keep new leaves from crisping at the edges as they unfurl. Propagate by cutting the rhizome into sections, each with at least one growing point and root.

common_name: Aurea Monkey Mask Monstera (Golden Variegated Adansonii)

planting.note: Pot rooted cuttings in spring into a chunky, well-drained aroid mix in a hanging basket or on a moss pole in bright, indirect light.

directions: This golden color form of the popular Swiss cheese vine trades the species' solid dark green for leaves streaked and sectored with buttery yellow, maintained true-to-type only by rooting cuttings taken from stable variegated stem sections rather than from seed. The characteristic oval, fenestrated leaves still develop their signature holes as the plant matures on a climbing support, though yellow-sectored leaf areas photosynthesize less efficiently and can be more prone to scorching in strong light. Provide bright, indirect light to encourage variegation without burning the pale tissue, and rotate the plant periodically since it will lean toward the brightest light source. Let the potting mix dry slightly between waterings and maintain warmth and humidity for the healthiest new growth.
